findings.text: Decision: the design's decisions go against the issue: RQTIE-1 requires that when two runs claim an issue at the same moment, exactly one proceeds — no qualification. The design's outside assumptions explicitly describe a scenario where both competing runs complete their note-post-and-read cycle before the other run's note has propagated, both see only their own note, and both return `{"acquired": true}`. Both runs therefore proceed, which cannot be true together with RQTIE-1. — has propagated, both see only their own note and both return `{"acquired": true}`. Closing [FIX IN DESIGN: ACCEPTED IF: The design does not accept a scenario where both runs return `{"acquired": true}` and proceed; or RQTIE-1 is itself qualified in the issue to permit a narrow propagation-window exception.]

answers: RLREDTEAM-2: done — The outside assumptions section of the design explicitly acknowledges GitHub's cross-connection comment visibility window. It states that a posted comment may not be visible to another client's read within a sub-second propagation window, creating a narrow residual race where both competing runs could complete their note-post-and-read cycle before the other's note propagates. It explains why this is accepted (closing the window requires sleep, which is prohibited by the determinism rules; the window is extremely narrow in practice), and that ADR-005 §5 will document it. This was added in round 3 and is present in the current design-draft.md.
